title: Colors, Backgrounds, and Borders
description: Master color models (HEX, RGB, HSL, alpha channels), background properties (gradients, images, sizing), and border/box-shadow styling for modern UI depth.

objectives.statement: Apply HEX, RGB, HSL, and semi-transparent alpha colors to UI elements.
Style containers with background gradients, border-radius, and elevation shadows.

content.title: Visual Depth with Color & Borders
content.hook: Colors evoke emotion and establish hierarchy, while borders and box-shadows give flat HTML elements tactile depth and visual structure.
content.context: CSS supports multiple color formats: HEX (`#3b82f6`), RGB/RGBA (`rgb(59 130 246 / 0.5)`), and HSL (`hsl(217 91% 60%)`). Combining semi-transparent colors with `border-radius` and `box-shadow` creates modern glass and card aesthetics.
goals: Compare HEX, RGB, and HSL color models.
Use alpha transparency for overlay backdrops and shadows.
Apply linear gradients, rounded corners (`border-radius`), and elevation (`box-shadow`).

content.title: The Anatomy of HSL Color
content.description: HSL format: Hue (0-360 deg on color wheel), Saturation (0% grayscale to 100% full color), Lightness (0% black to 50% pure color to 100% white).

content.prompt: Which CSS background declaration creates a semi-transparent dark overlay using RGBA color notation?
options: All three options produce valid 50% transparent black backgrounds in modern CSS
None of these, CSS requires opacity: 0.5 on the parent container

validation.expected: All three options produce valid 50% transparent black backgrounds in modern CSS

feedback.correct: Spot on! Modern CSS supports alpha channels in RGB, HSL, and 8-digit HEX syntax. All three create a 50% semi-transparent black overlay without affecting child text opacity.
feedback.incorrect: All three formats (RGB with alpha, 8-digit HEX with alpha, and HSL with alpha) are fully valid standard CSS alpha color notations.

content.title: Build a Styled Pricing Card
content.prompt:
Style the `.card` container:
1. Give it a subtle linear gradient background: `background: linear-gradient(135deg, #ffffff, #f1f5f9)`.
2. Add a `border: 1px solid #e2e8f0` and `border-radius: 12px`.
3. Add elevation depth with `box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)`.
4. Style `.badge` with `background-color: #dbeafe`, `color: #1e40af`, and `border-radius: 9999px`.

testCases.description: .badge must have pill rounded corners (border-radius > 100px or 9999px)
.badge must have light blue background and dark blue text

feedback.correct: Beautiful card craftsmanship! You combined gradient backgrounds, rounded corners, pill badges, and soft elevation shadows.
feedback.incorrect: Review your rules: set gradient background, border, radius, and shadow on `.card`, and pill radius with background/color on `.badge`.

hints.content: Add `background: linear-gradient(135deg, #ffffff, #f1f5f9); border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);` to `.card`.

content.prompt: Why is setting background color with alpha transparency (e.g. `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)`) preferred over setting `opacity: 0.5` on a parent modal element?

feedback.correct: Great insight! The `opacity` property makes the parent AND all child elements (including text, icons, and buttons) semi-transparent, whereas alpha background colors apply transparency strictly to the background layer while keeping text crisp and opaque.
feedback.incorrect: Think about how the opacity property affects child text and content inside a container versus alpha background colors.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Colors & Elevation
takeaways: Modern CSS supports HEX, RGB, and HSL color models with alpha transparency channels.
Alpha color channels adjust background opacity without fading child text and content.
border-radius creates rounded corners and pill badges (using border-radius: 9999px).
box-shadow adds realistic visual elevation depth to floating UI cards and modals.
